key_insight: A hierarchical multilevel Monte Carlo neural critic removes the bias-cost bottleneck in primal-dual actor-critic learning, enabling order-optimal convergence for average-reward CMDPs.
engineering_relevance: This makes safe reinforcement learning more practical for safety-critical systems by providing neural-critic guarantees for both reward optimization and constraint satisfaction without requiring prior mixing-time knowledge.
method: Use a hierarchical MLMC neural critic to debias estimates across both trajectory sampling and critic optimization.
Combine the critic with a primal-dual natural actor-critic framework for average-reward CMDPs.
Leverage NTK-based analysis to achieve long-run critic accuracy at only logarithmic expected sample cost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports O(T^{-1/2}) convergence for both optimality gap and constraint violation, establishing the first order-optimal guarantees for infinite-horizon average-reward CMDPs with neural critics.
watch_item: The approach relies on NTK-style assumptions and a hierarchical MLMC implementation, so practical performance may depend on model width, tuning, and the cost of multilevel critic optimization.
paper_title: Hierarchical Multilevel Monte Carlo for Order-Optimal Neural Actor-Critic in Average-Reward CMDPs
